title: Router selection trace
description: One record per selection decision. Traces are what make the confusion matrix in docs/SELECTION-SLO.md possible. They deliberately record a case identifier rather than the utterance text: committed evidence must not carry raw prompts, because a prompt can contain material the data boundary excludes from this repository.

case_id.description: Identifier of the selection case. NOT the utterance text — see the description above.

complexity_class.description: Classified before ranking. MULTI never becomes a silent multi-skill run; it asks or offers a documented workflow.

nav_path.description: The job-tree branch narrowed to before ranking. Absent when the router searched globally.

candidates.description: Ranked candidates considered. Present even when the decision was refuse, because what was considered is part of why.

excluded_by.description: Populated when a candidate was removed by a conflict rule, a refuse tag, or a disabled-skill setting.

margin.description: Score gap between the top two candidates. The quantity that decides top-1 versus ask, and the one to inspect first when selection degrades.

decision.description: forced = the user named a skill explicitly. A forced selection still honours refuse tags and the data boundary.

selected_id.description: Present for top_1 and forced. Absent for ask and refuse.

refuse_reason.description: Required when decision is refuse. Enumerated so refusal correctness can be counted rather than read.

human_role_named.description: For a human_only refusal, whether the accountable role was named. A refusal that does not say who should do it is incomplete.

contexts_attached.description: Context ids attached AFTER selection. Contexts are never candidates; their presence here and absence from `candidates` is the invariant that keeps them out of the ranking.

reason_code.description: Short machine-comparable reason, e.g. clear_margin, close_top_2, refuse_human_only, forced_by_user, multi_offered_workflow.

alias_resolved_from.description: Set when the request named a retired id. If this is present AND a live id also matched, that is a double-activation defect.
